Maritime NDT training in Newport News: the short answer

Maritime and shipbuilding NDT training for Newport News employers and technicians is delivered by Atlantis NDT as live online classes or onsite at your facility, under ASNT Level III oversight. Courses follow ASNT SNT-TC-1A and focus on what hull and structural work actually uses: VT, MT, UT, PAUT, RT and PT on thick-section welded steel. Navy work then adds NAVSEA qualification inside the employer's programme. Atlantis has no Newport News training centre; quotes are on request.

This page is about the hull, structure and outfitting side of shipbuilding: the miles of plate and erection welds that turn steel into a carrier or a submarine hull, the piping and foundations fitted inside it, and the fabricators who supply modules and components to the yard. Reactor plant and commercial nuclear examinations are a different discipline with different owners, and they are covered on the separate nuclear NDT training in Newport News page. If you are a welder, fitter or veteran trying to work out how to move into shipyard inspection on the Peninsula, or a fabricator whose customer has just asked for NAVSEA-compliant examination records, this is the right page.

To start, request a maritime NDT training quote for Newport News with your methods, levels and number of technicians.

Shipbuilding NDT work in Newport News

Newport News is dominated by one employer: Newport News Shipbuilding, a division of HII, the builder of the Navy's nuclear-powered aircraft carriers and co-builder, with General Dynamics Electric Boat, of the Virginia-class and Columbia-class submarines. From an examination point of view, what matters is not the nuclear propulsion plant but the sheer volume of structural welding around it.

Carrier hull and superstructure

A carrier is built as large pre-outfitted modules ("superlifts") that are assembled in the dry dock. Every module is full of welds made in the shops and on the platen, and every lift creates erection joints that are made in the dock, often in thick plate, in awkward positions and against a schedule. Those joints are where volumetric examination concentrates: ultrasonic testing on full-penetration butt and tee joints, radiography where the specification calls for a permanent image, and magnetic particle testing on the fillet and partial-penetration welds that hold stiffeners, foundations and attachments to the hull.

Submarine pressure hull

Submarine hull construction uses high-strength steels and some of the most demanding weld quality requirements in industry, because the pressure hull is the boundary between the crew and the sea. Examination of hull welds, penetrations and hull-attached structure is tightly specified, heavily documented and audited by the Navy's technical authority. Submarine modules move between the two builders, so examination records travel with the hardware.

Piping, outfitting and foundations

Inside the hull sit thousands of piping systems in carbon steel, corrosion-resistant steel and copper-nickel, plus machinery foundations and ventilation. Piping welds take radiography or ultrasonic examination depending on system class, and non-magnetic materials take penetrant testing rather than MT. Visual examination is everywhere: fit-up, in-process and final.

The supplier base and the port

Around the yard sits a base of fabricators, machine shops, module builders and inspection service companies across the Peninsula and Hampton Roads, many of them supplying the submarine industrial base. The Port of Virginia's Newport News Marine Terminal and the waterfront industries add structural and lifting-equipment inspection. For the repair-yard market across the water, see maritime NDT training in Norfolk.

Methods used on hull and structural work in Newport News

MethodShipbuilding application in Newport NewsCode / standard usually invoked
VTFit-up, in-process and final weld inspection on every module; weld profile, undercut, porosity and dimensional checksNAVSEA T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 (method); MIL-STD-1689 (surface ship structure); MIL-STD-2035 (acceptance)
MTFillet, tee and attachment welds on ferritic hull structure; back-gouge and excavation checks before repair weldingNAVSEA 271; MIL-STD-2035; ASTM E1444 for technique reference
UT (conventional)Full-penetration butt and tee joints in thick plate, lamination checks before welding, thickness verificationNAVSEA 271; MIL-STD-2035; AWS D1.1 on non-naval structural work
PAUTErection joints in the dock where radiography would stop other trades; encoded records for reviewable acceptanceWhere the contract and NAVSEA permit; ASME Section V Article 4 on commercial work
TOFDSizing support on thick-section joints alongside PAUTProject specification
RTPiping system welds and structural joints where a permanent image is specified; often shot off-shift to clear radiation areasNAVSEA 271; MIL-STD-2035
PTCorrosion-resistant steel and copper-nickel piping, aluminium and other non-magnetic fittingsNAVSEA 271; MIL-STD-2035
ETSurface crack detection through coatings, heat exchanger tubing on auxiliary systemsProcedure-specific; less common on new-construction structure

Local method spotlight: phased array UT on erection joints. In a busy dry dock, radiography means clearing an area, stopping other trades and waiting for film or digital images to be read. Ultrasonic examination, and especially encoded phased array, lets the joint be examined while work continues nearby and produces a record that can be re-analysed. That is why shipyards keep building PAUT capacity, and why a Newport News technician with UT Level II plus PAUT is more employable than one with surface methods alone. Our UT Level II course and phased array training are the usual next steps after MT Level II.

Which certification scheme Newport News shipbuilding employers expect

SchemeWho requires itDoes SNT-TC-1A training fit?
ASNT SNT-TC-1ACommercial fabricators, inspection companies, port and terminal work, and the base of many employer written practicesYes. Atlantis trains to SNT-TC-1A; the employer certifies under its written practice.
NAVSEA T9074-AS-GIB-010/271Naval new construction and repair, the yard and its subcontractors performing NDT on Navy workPartly. Method training is the foundation, but 271 sets its own qualification and examination requirements, administered through the employer's NAVSEA-compliant programme. Our courses do not grant 271 qualification.
ABS / classification society rulesCommercial vessels and offshore structures built or repaired to classGenerally yes. Class rules usually accept personnel certified to a recognised scheme such as SNT-TC-1A; the surveyor reviews certifications and procedures.
AWS D1.1 / D1.6Structural steel and stainless fabrication outside the naval specification, including shore-side structuresYes. D1.1 refers to SNT-TC-1A-based qualification of NDT personnel.
AWS CWISome employers for welding inspection rolesNot offered by Atlantis. CWI is a separate AWS certification; mentioned only because Peninsula job postings sometimes list it.
ISO 9712Foreign-flag and international ownersNot offered. Context only.

The pattern for a Peninsula technician: earn solid SNT-TC-1A certifications in VT, MT and UT, then join an employer whose programme qualifies you for NAVSEA scope. For a fabricator: make sure your written practice, procedures and records will satisfy both a class surveyor and a Navy or prime-contractor audit before bidding naval work.

The SNT-TC-1A path, step by step, for a shipyard technician

  1. Employer written practice. Your employer's written practice sets the training, experience, exam and recertification rules for each method and level. If the company does naval work, it will also reference the NAVSEA qualification requirements.
  2. Classroom training per method, typically VT and MT first, then UT. Use our training requirements matrix for the SNT-TC-1A recommended hours rather than guessing.
  3. On-the-job experience, documented and supervised. Shipyard experience logs should show weld types, joint geometries, materials and thicknesses, which is exactly what a later employer will ask about.
  4. General, specific and practical exams, administered under a Level III, with the practical on real weld specimens.
  5. Vision examination, near vision and colour contrast as required.
  6. Written certification by the employer.
  7. NAVSEA qualification where you will examine Navy work, through the employer's programme.
  8. Recertification on the interval set by the written practice, with continuing evidence of work in the method.

Background on the scheme is on our SNT-TC-1A certification page; level-by-level detail is on the Level II path.

Radiation licensing, TWIC and yard access

Radiography with radioactive sources in Virginia is licensed by the Virginia Department of Health's Radioactive Materials Program, because Virginia has been an NRC Agreement State since 2009. Radiographers must meet the state's radiographer training and certification requirements, which follow the federal industrial radiography rules. In a shipyard, radiography is often scheduled off-shift so that radiation areas can be barricaded without stopping other trades; crews should expect night and weekend work. Where work is on a federal installation under exclusive federal jurisdiction, NRC reciprocity can apply. Your radiation safety officer confirms which rules govern each job.

Access is a separate gate. The yard issues its own badges and site training. Marine terminals and other facilities regulated under the Maritime Transportation Security Act require a Transportation Worker Identification Credential (TWIC) for unescorted access. Navy installations require base-access credentials and, for some work, citizenship or security vetting. Build those lead times into any hiring or training plan.

How Atlantis delivers maritime NDT training to Newport News crews

  • Onsite at your shop or yard facility. An ASNT Level III-led cohort using your equipment, your weld specimens and your procedures. For a fabricator or inspection company, this keeps practical exams and records exactly where an auditor expects them.
  • Live online. Instructor-led theory and specific-exam preparation for technicians across the Peninsula and Hampton Roads, scheduled around shift patterns. See online NDT training.
  • Blended. Theory online; practical sessions and exams onsite, timed around module lifts, dock milestones and sea trials.

Shipyard emphasis we can build into a cohort: reading weld symbols and NAVSEA drawings, the difference between method procedures and acceptance standards, MT on curved and stiffened plate, UT on tee joints and thick plate, PT on copper-nickel and corrosion-resistant steel piping, and record-keeping that a prime contractor will accept. Ask about onsite maritime NDT training for your Newport News crew. Multi-site and multi-method programmes run through corporate NDT training, and our marine corporate training and defense corporate training pages describe sector cohorts.

Written practices and Level III services for Peninsula shipbuilding suppliers

When a fabricator moves from commercial work into the naval supply chain, the first audit usually finds the same gaps: a written practice copied from a template that does not match the company's methods, missing NAVSEA provisions, procedures that cite the wrong acceptance standard, no defined relationship with a Level III, and training and experience records that cannot be traced. Each finding delays approval.

  • Written practice development and review to SNT-TC-1A, with notes on NAVSEA and class expectations. See NDT written practice development.
  • Level III services: procedure and technique review, exam development and administration, and pre-audit records checks.
  • Supplier readiness reviews before a prime-contractor or Navy audit.

For engineering and inspection consulting on the Peninsula, see maritime NDT consulting in Newport News and NDT consulting in Newport News. To get a reviewer on your documents, book a Level III consultation.

Practise before the practical exam

The Practical NDT simulator lets trainees rehearse 12 NDT methods in five 3D environments, including a welding workshop that maps closely to shipyard weld examination. Use it to drill MT technique, UT scan patterns and indication recognition before time on real equipment. It is practice only and does not replace hands-on training or the practical exam on real specimens. Local entry: Practical NDT Newport News.

Local options compared

  • The Apprentice School at Newport News Shipbuilding: a paid, multi-year apprenticeship that includes a Non-Destructive Tester trade covering RT, MT, PT, UT, ET and VT with codes and quality standards. For anyone who wants to work at the yard and can commit, it is the most direct route. It is an employer programme with competitive entry, not a public course.
  • Virginia Peninsula Community College and Tidewater-area colleges: strong welding programmes, which are a common feeder into NDT on the Peninsula. Check current catalogues for any NDT-specific coursework.
  • Brightpoint Community College (formerly John Tyler, near Richmond) has a long history of NDT coursework in its engineering technology programmes.
  • Maritime-focused and national training providers: some run scheduled public courses at their own centres or online; at least one maritime NDT training provider has announced an expansion into Hampton Roads.
  • Atlantis NDT: SNT-TC-1A training for employers and crews, live online or onsite, plus written practice and Level III services. Not the right fit if you need NAVSEA qualification issued independently of an employer, because no outside provider can do that.

For the state-wide view, see NDT training in Virginia, and for the city-wide view, NDT training in Newport News.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, who oversees course content, practical exams and, where your written practice designates Atlantis as an outside agency, exam administration.

Frequently asked questions about maritime NDT training in Newport News

How do I become a shipyard NDT technician in Newport News?

Two routes work. Apply to the shipyard's Apprentice School for the Non-Destructive Tester trade, or earn SNT-TC-1A certifications (VT, MT, then UT) through an employer or training provider and join a contractor or supplier doing naval or commercial marine work. Either way, NAVSEA qualification comes through the employer's programme.

Does Atlantis training count for NAVSEA work?

It counts as method training that an employer can credit under its programme, but NAVSEA T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 qualification is administered by the employer or yard, not granted by an outside course.

Can I take shipbuilding NDT training online in Virginia?

Theory and exam preparation, yes, through live online classes. Practical training and the practical exam need real equipment and weld specimens, which we deliver onsite at the employer's facility.

Which NDT method should I learn first for shipyard work?

Visual testing and magnetic particle testing are where most shipyard examiners start, because they cover the largest volume of welds. Ultrasonic testing, then phased array, is the most valuable next step.

Can a welder move into NDT at a shipyard?

Yes, and it is one of the most common routes on the Peninsula. Welders already read weld symbols and understand discontinuities. See welder to NDT technician without a degree.

What is MIL-STD-2035?

It is the Navy standard that sets acceptance criteria for NDT on naval work, used together with the NAVSEA method and qualification requirements. Training teaches you to apply acceptance criteria correctly; the contract determines which document governs.

Do I need TWIC to work as an NDT technician in Newport News?

You need TWIC for unescorted access to MTSA-regulated marine facilities such as port terminals. Shipyard and Navy base access use their own credentials. Many marine NDT employers ask new hires to hold TWIC.

Do I need a radiography licence in Virginia?

Your employer needs a radioactive materials licence from the Virginia Department of Health, and you must meet the state's radiographer certification and training requirements. NDT method certification is separate.

How long does UT Level II training take?

The employer's written practice sets the classroom hours and experience, using SNT-TC-1A as the reference. Our training requirements matrix lists the recommended minimums; you can rehearse with UT Level 2 practice questions.

What does maritime NDT training cost in Newport News?

Atlantis quotes on request. The quote depends on methods, levels, group size, online versus onsite delivery, and whether written practice or Level III work is included. Cohort and onsite quotes come back within one business day.

Can I use the GI Bill or WIOA for NDT training?

Those programmes generally require an approved school or listed eligible training provider. Atlantis does not claim that status, so check provider lists first. Employer-paid training is the common alternative. Veterans should also read veterans transitioning into NDT.

How is this different from the nuclear NDT page for Newport News?

This page covers hull, structural, piping and outfitting examination. The nuclear NDT training in Newport News page covers reactor plant scope, commercial nuclear ISI and the nuclear supply chain.
